# opencode-model-fallback

An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) plugin that keeps a session alive when the
model it is using starts failing. When a provider rate-limits the request or the
free-tier quota runs out, the plugin **switches the session to the next model in
a configurable fallback chain** and resumes the turn instead of just letting the
request fail.

It was written for the free OpenCode model tier (where the free usage limit is a
non-retryable `provider.quota` error) but is generic: the chain can point at any
providers/models you have configured.

---

## Features

- **Two switch mechanisms, on purpose:**
  1. **`retry` hook** — for failures OpenCode already wants to retry (HTTP 429,
     provider-internal/transport errors). The plugin benches the current model,
     switches the session and retries immediately.
  2. **Event stream** — for *terminal* failures the retry hook never sees. The
     important one is the free-tier usage limit, emitted as
     `provider.quota`. The plugin listens for session failure events, benches +
     switches the model, then **resumes** the turn.
- **Fallback chain** — an ordered list of `{providerID, id}` entries. The plugin
  picks the first healthy, not-benched, not-already-tried entry. Entries whose id
  ends in `-free` are treated as the free tier: while the session is already on a
  paid entry, picking stays inside the paid section, so a paid fallback never
  silently downgrades to a healthy free model.
- **Per-model cooldown / bench** with exponential penalty for consecutive
  failures, plus a longer cooldown for auth failures.
- **Cross-instance de-duplication** — an exclusive lock file keyed by
  session+failure ensures only one copy switches when OpenCode loads the plugin
  more than once (global discovery + per-process), plus in-process debounce so a
  burst of failure events triggers a single switch.
- **Smart classification** — never switches on content-filter, genuine invalid
  requests, unsupported operations or aborts; *does* switch on
  deprecated/unknown/no-longer-available models (a model problem, not a request
  problem).
- **Restores the chain head on a new prompt** so a new turn starts from the
  preferred (usually free) model again.
- **Zero dependencies** — only Node built-ins (`fs`, `os`, `path`).
- **Live config reload** — edits to `model-fallback.json` are picked up without
  restarting.

---

## Requirements

- OpenCode V2 (server `>= 2.0.21`).
- No install-time dependencies. Tests use [Bun](https://bun.sh), the runtime
  OpenCode uses.

---

## Install

### Option A — copy the folder (simplest)

OpenCode auto-discovers plugins under the global plugins directory:

```
~/.config/opencode/plugins/<anything>/index.js
```

So:

1. Copy this folder to `~/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-model-fallback/`
   (or run the bundled installer, see Option C).
2. Put a config at `~/.config/opencode/model-fallback.json`
   (copy `model-fallback.example.json` and edit the chain).
3. Restart OpenCode.

### Option B — reference it by path or as a package

In `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    // local directory
    "/home/me/opencode-model-fallback",
    // or a file URL
    // "file:///home/me/opencode-model-fallback",
    // or a published npm package
    // "opencode-model-fallback",
    // or a pinned version
    // "opencode-model-fallback@1.0.0"
  ]
}
```

> If you install by directory (Option A) do **not** also add it to `plugins` —
> global plugins are auto-discovered, and listing it too can load it twice.

### Option C — installer script

```sh
./install.sh
# or into a custom config dir:
OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR=/path/to/opencode-config ./install.sh
```

`install.sh` copies the plugin into
`$CONFIG_DIR/plugins/opencode-model-fallback/` and creates
`$CONFIG_DIR/model-fallback.json` from the example **only if one does not already
exist** (your chain is never overwritten). `uninstall.sh` removes the plugin
directory and leaves the config file in place.

---

## Configuration

The plugin looks for a config in this order (first match wins):

1. `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR/model-fallback.json`
2. `~/.config/opencode/model-fallback.json`
3. `<project>/.opencode/model-fallback.json`

```jsonc
{
  "enabled": true,
  // How long a failed model is benched, in ms.
  "cooldownMs": 1800000,
  // Upper bound for the exponential bench, in ms.
  "cooldownMaxMs": 21600000,
  // Bench multiplier applied for consecutive failures of the same model.
  "consecutivePenalty": 2,
  // Minimum bench for auth failures (401/403/etc.).
  "authCooldownMs": 7200000,
  // Switch back to chain[0] on the next real user prompt (if healthy).
  "restoreChainHeadOnNewPrompt": true,
  // Re-read the config file every N ms.
  "reloadMs": 15000,
  // Collapse a burst of failure events (step.failed + execution.failed + error)
  // into one switch.
  "eventDebounceMs": 1200,
  // Upper bound on the per-session handling throttle, in ms. A successful
  // switch clears it, so a genuine failure on the newly selected model is
  // handled right away and the chain keeps advancing instead of stalling.
  "eventThrottleMs": 5000,
  // Optional log file. A leading "~/" is expanded to your home directory.
  // Empty string = console only (OpenCode captures console output).
  "logFile": "~/.local/share/opencode/log/model-fallback.log",
  // Ordered fallback chain: free models first, then paid models. Among the paid
  // entries the first one is preferred.
  "chain": [
    { "providerID": "opencode", "id": "step-5-preview-free" },
    { "providerID": "opencode", "id": "longcat-2.5-preview-free" },
    { "providerID": "opencode-go", "id": "step-5-preview-free" },
    { "providerID": "opencode-go", "id": "longcat-2.5-preview-free" },
    { "providerID": "opencode-go", "id": "deepseek-v4-flash" },
    { "providerID": "opencode-go", "id": "deepseek-v4.1-flash" },
    { "providerID": "opencode-go", "id": "deepseek-v4-pro" }
  ]
}
```

Only `chain` is really required; everything else falls back to the defaults
shown above. The chain is validated at load time (`{providerID, id}` objects) —
an invalid file logs an error and the previous config is kept.

---

## How it works

```
provider failure
      │
      ├── retryable (429, provider-internal, transport, …)
      │        └─ retry hook ──▶ bench current ─▶ switch ─▶ retry (delay 0)
      │
      └── terminal (quota, auth, invalid-output, …)
               └─ session.*.failed event ──▶ classify ─▶ bench current
                       ─▶ switch ─▶ schedule resume (session.prompt {resume:true})
```

The classifier maps OpenCode's structured error types
(`provider.rate-limit`, `provider.quota`, `provider.auth`, `provider.no-route`,
`provider.invalid-output`, …) to "switch", and explicitly ignores
`provider.content-filter`, `provider.invalid-request`,
`provider.unsupported-operation` and `aborted`. Messages that indicate a
retired/deprecated/unknown model override the "invalid request" verdict and are
treated as switch-worthy.

---

## Logging & troubleshooting

Set `logFile` to get a dedicated log (recommended). Lines look like:

```
[2026-10-12T13:40:49.000Z] armed (v1.0.2): chain=7 head=opencode/step-5-preview-free tail=opencode/deepseek-v4-pro
[2026-10-12T13:41:02.000Z] config loaded from /home/me/.config/opencode/model-fallback.json (chain=7)
[2026-10-12T13:41:10.000Z] switch ses_ed194bf7 opencode/step-5-preview-free -> opencode/ling-3.1-flash-free (retry rate status=429 streak=1 bench=1800s)
[2026-10-12T13:41:10.000Z] switch ses_ed194bf7 opencode/space-bunny-free -> opencode/step-5-preview-free (event rate type=provider.invalid-output streak=1 bench=1800s)
[2026-10-12T13:41:10.000Z] resumed ses_ed194bf7
```

- `armed: chain=0` → no config found; check the search paths above.
- `chain provider X: NOT FOUND in the provider list` → that provider isn't
  configured in OpenCode; entries for it are skipped.
- `event: no fallback left …` → every chain entry is benched/tried; the plugin
  waits out the cooldown and resumes.
- When `logFile` is empty, the same lines go to stdout, which OpenCode records in
  its own log (`~/.local/share/opencode/log/`).

---

## Development

```sh
bun test/test.mjs   # or: bun run test
```

The harness mocks the OpenCode plugin context and drives both mechanisms; it
exits non-zero on the first failure. It covers rate/auth retries, chain
advancing, transient-error ignoring, the quota event path (+ resume), event
de-duplication, content-filter/invalid-request non-switching, deprecated-model
switching, cross-instance claim locking, paid-section preference (a paid model
falls back to the first paid model, never to a healthy free one) and cascade
continuation (a failure on the just-switched-to model is handled immediately
rather than stalling the chain).

---

## Packaging / using on another machine

- **Folder**: copy this directory over and run `install.sh`.
- **Tarball**: `npm pack` (or `tar czf`) and extract on the target, then
  `install.sh`.
- **npm**: publish with `npm publish` (adjust `name`/`license` first), then add
  `"opencode-model-fallback"` to your `plugins` array or let OpenCode resolve it.

## Uninstall

```sh
./uninstall.sh
```

Then delete `~/.config/opencode/model-fallback.json` if you no longer want it.

## Privacy

The plugin makes **no network requests and collects no telemetry**. It only
reads your local `model-fallback.json`, talks to your local OpenCode server, and
— if `logFile` is configured — appends to a local file. Nothing leaves your
machine.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented here.
This project follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## [1.0.2] - 2026-10-12

### Changed
- Startup log now includes the plugin version (`armed (v1.0.2): …`) so the
  version loaded by a running server can be confirmed from the log.

## [1.0.1] - 2026-10-12

### Added
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `SECURITY.md`.
- Dependabot configuration for GitHub Actions.

### Changed
- CI and release workflows pin actions to commit SHAs and use least-privilege
  `permissions`.
- `release.yml`: tests gate an automatic tag + GitHub Release on a version bump;
  npm publishing is opt-in and tokenless via OIDC Trusted Publishing.
- Commits use a GitHub noreply identity; no personal email is published.
- Example/default chain: free models first, then paid models with
  `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash` first among them.

### Fixed
- Free→paid fallback stalled after a single step. Failure de-duplication keyed
  only on the error message, so a failure on the model just switched to (usually
  the same "rate limit" text) was mistaken for a duplicate and swallowed. The
  claim key now includes the current model and a successful switch clears the
  per-session throttle, so the chain keeps descending within one turn and
  actually reaches the paid section.
- A failure on a paid model could downgrade the session to a healthy free model.
  `pick` now keeps a session that is already on a paid entry inside the paid
  section until the whole paid section is benched.

## [1.0.0] - 2026-10-12

### Added
- Initial release.
- Fallback chain of `{providerID, id}` models, tried in order.
- `retry` hook: switches and retries on retryable provider failures (HTTP 429,
  provider-internal/transport errors).
- Event-stream handler: switches and **resumes** the turn on terminal failures
  the retry hook never sees — notably the free-tier usage limit
  (`provider.quota`).
- Structured-error classifier that never switches on content-filter, genuine
  invalid requests, unsupported operations or aborts, but does switch on
  deprecated/retired/unknown models.
- Per-model cooldown with exponential penalty and a longer auth cooldown.
- Cross-instance/cross-process claim locking plus in-process event debounce and
  throttle to avoid duplicate switches.
- Optional chained file logging (with `~/` expansion) and live config reload.
- Automatic return to the chain head on a new user prompt.
- Zero runtime dependencies (Node built-ins only).
- Self-test harness (`bun test/test.mjs`), installer/uninstaller scripts, and a
  portable example config.

# Contributing

Thanks for helping improve `opencode-model-fallback`. This is a small, focused
plugin; the goal is to keep it dependency-free, predictable and easy to audit.

## Prerequisites

- [Bun](https://bun.sh) — the runtime OpenCode uses and the one the tests run on.
- No other dependencies; the plugin uses only Node built-ins (`fs`, `os`, `path`).

## Development loop

```sh
git clone https://github.com/mino29/opencode-model-fallback.git
cd opencode-model-fallback
bun test/test.mjs      # or: bun run test
```

`test/test.mjs` mocks the OpenCode plugin context (`model.list`, `provider.list`,
`session.hook/get/switchModel/prompt`, `event.subscribe`) and drives both switch
mechanisms — the native `retry` hook and the failure-event stream. It exits
non-zero on the first failed assertion, so it works as a CI gate as-is.

When you change behavior, add or update a test case. Keep the two mechanisms
independent: the retry hook handles retryable failures, the event stream handles
terminal ones (e.g. the free-tier `provider.quota` limit) that the hook never
sees.

## Privacy & secret hygiene

This project is intentionally privacy-respecting. Please keep it that way:

- **Never commit secrets.** No API keys, tokens, tokens-in-URLs, or
  `.git-credentials`. The plugin needs none.
- **No personal data.** Don't hardcode home directories, usernames or email
  addresses. Use `os.homedir()` / `~` expansion and make paths configurable.
- **Commits use a private identity.** This repository is configured to commit as
  `42552577+mino29@users.noreply.github.com`. If you commit with a real address,
  set it per-repo:

  ```sh
  git config user.email "42552577+mino29@users.noreply.github.com"
  ```
- **The plugin stays offline.** It must not make network requests or collect
  telemetry. It only reads the local config, talks to the local OpenCode server,
  and writes local logs.

## Commit & PR conventions

- Small, self-contained commits with an imperative subject
  (`switch: retry when the chain head is benched`, `docs: ...`).
- Describe the failure mode being fixed and how you verified it. Live evidence
  (a log line) is ideal.
- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) must be green. Actions are pinned to commit
  SHAs; Dependabot will keep them fresh.

## Release process

Releases are automated by `.github/workflows/release.yml`:

1. Bump `version` in `package.json` and add a matching `CHANGELOG.md` entry.
2. Merge to `main`.
3. The workflow re-runs the tests, and — if `v<version>` does not already exist —
   creates an annotated tag, pushes it, and publishes a GitHub Release with
   generated notes.

Publishing to npm is **opt-in and tokenless**. To enable it, configure a
[Trusted Publisher](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers) on npmjs.com for
this repo/workflow and set the repository variable `NPM_PUBLISH=true`. No
`NPM_TOKEN` secret is ever stored; GitHub mints a short-lived OIDC token and the
package is published with build provenance.

## Reporting security issues

Please do not open a public issue for vulnerabilities — see
[SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md).

# Security Policy

## Supported versions

The latest `1.x` release receives security fixes.

| Version | Supported |
| ------- | --------- |
| 1.x     | ✅        |
| < 1.0   | ❌        |

## Reporting a vulnerability

**Please do not report security issues in public issues, discussions or PRs.**

Use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting: go to the repository's
**Security** tab and choose **Report a vulnerability**. That opens a private
advisory visible only to the maintainers. If you cannot use that flow, contact
the maintainer privately via the GitHub profile [@mino29](https://github.com/mino29).

Please include:

- what the issue is and its impact,
- steps or a proof of concept to reproduce it,
- the affected version and environment.

You can expect an acknowledgement within a few days. Coordinated disclosure is
appreciated; we will credit you in the advisory unless you prefer otherwise.

## Scope and design notes

`opencode-model-fallback` is a local OpenCode plugin. Its security-relevant
properties are deliberately small:

- **No network access.** The plugin makes no outbound requests and collects no
  telemetry. It calls only the local OpenCode plugin API and reads/writes local
  files.
- **No secrets.** It stores no credentials and reads none. Provider credentials
  are handled entirely by OpenCode.
- **Local inputs only.** It reads `model-fallback.json` (from
  `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`, `~/.config/opencode`, or `<project>/.opencode`) and,
  if `logFile` is set, appends log lines to that path. Treat the config file and
  log path as you would any other local file you own.
- **Cross-process lock files** are created under the OS temp directory
  (`os.tmpdir()/opencode-model-fallback-locks`) solely to de-duplicate switches
  between concurrently loaded plugin copies.

Supply-chain hardening of the repository itself:

- Workflow actions are pinned to commit SHAs and kept current by Dependabot.
- Workflows run with least-privilege `permissions`; npm publishing is opt-in and
  uses OIDC Trusted Publishing (no long-lived tokens).
- Commits use a GitHub noreply identity, so no personal email is published.
